faq.title: What students and clients ask first
faq.q1: Is this legal for my permit?
faq.a1: Kontrak engages you as an employee, not as a freelancer. A §16b student permit generally allows employment within 140 full or 280 half days a year. We record your permit wording at sign-up and filter every brief against it. Your Ausländerbehörde has the final word on your individual permit.
faq.q2: Do students ever pay to find work?
faq.a2: No. Finding work is free and your first job carries no fee. After that, 5% is taken from money already paid to you. No earnings in a month means no fee.
faq.a3: Only when you are paid. We take 5% of the amount released to you from your second job onwards, plus 3% if you chose the optional boost. Clients post briefs for free.
faq.q4: What if I run out of days?
faq.a4: Bids that need more days or hours than you have left are blocked before you can send them. Hours that would go over a limit cannot be logged either. Your day account resets on 1 January.
faq.q5: What happens to the money if the client disappears?
faq.a5: The client pays the fee into escrow before you start, and it stays there until the client signs off. In this prototype, escrow and payouts are simulated. A live version would hold funds with a licensed payment provider.
faq.q6: What is a Day-Cap Safe brief?
faq.a6: A brief whose scoped hours fit a 20-hour week across its timeline, that pays at least the €13.90 statutory minimum per hour, and that sits under German law. Your own day account is checked again when you bid.
faq.a7: Every client gives a Handelsregister number at sign-up. In this prototype the check is simulated: HRB and HRA numbers pass, anything else goes to manual review by the Kontrak team.
faq.q8: Does this replace advice from my Ausländerbehörde?
faq.a8: No. Kontrak tracks the limits and blocks work that would break them, but your Ausländerbehörde and the wording on your permit decide your case. Ask them if you are unsure.
